title: Timed Mixed Lab Set A

header.html: All five domains (weighted like the exam: Environment, Configuration and Security 4 tasks, Application Design and Build 3, Application Deployment 3, Services and Networking 3, Observability and Maintenance 3)
review of every domain under time pressure
Kubernetes v1.37.0; every task in this set was executed and validated in Modules 1 to 16 (setup, failing check, solution, passing check, wrong answers rejected)

html:
1How to use this set

  1. Reset: make sure the lab cluster is healthy (kubectl get nodes shows three Ready nodes).
  2. Start a 120-minute timer. Allowed documentation only: kubernetes.io/docs and blog, helm.sh/docs.
  3. For each task, prepare its starting state with python run_labs.py --setup <lab-id> (it also prints the task), then solve it as you would on the exam.
  4. Score yourself with python run_labs.py --check <lab-id>. A task is all-or-nothing, like the exam's scoring.
  5. Pass mark: 66% of the points.

Honest note: this set reuses tasks from the module labs, so you have seen their wording before. Use it as a timed rehearsal of speed and routine, then use the killer.sh simulator for tasks you have never seen.

2Tasks

Set size: 16 tasks, 109 points in total. Pass mark: 66%, which is 72 points. Suggested time: 120 minutes (the labs' own time estimates add up to 117 minutes). Do the tasks in order, flag what you skip, and check your work as you would on the exam.

Task 1 (Environment, 6 points, about 7 minutes) m09-01-configmap-env-volume

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace cfg, create a ConfigMap app-config with the keys LOG_LEVEL=debug and color=blue. Create a Pod cfgpod (image busybox:1.36, command sleep 3600) that:

  • gets the environment variable LOG_LEVEL from the ConfigMap key of the same name (not a hard-coded value), and
  • mounts the whole ConfigMap as files in the directory /etc/app.

Task 2 (Environment, 8 points, about 8 minutes) m11-03-role-rolebinding

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace auth, the ServiceAccount app-sa exists. Create a Role named pod-reader that allows only get, list and watch on Pods, and a RoleBinding named read-pods that gives this Role to app-sa. Afterwards the ServiceAccount must be able to list Pods in auth but not delete them, and must not be able to list Pods in the namespace default.

Task 3 (Environment, 7 points, about 7 minutes) m10-03-resource-quota

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace quota, create a ResourceQuota named team-quota that allows at most 3 Pods, 500m of total CPU requests and 1Gi of total memory limits. Then create a Deployment web (image nginx:alpine, 2 replicas) whose Pods each request 100m CPU and have a memory limit of 256Mi, so that both replicas are Ready within the quota.

Task 4 (Environment, 8 points, about 9 minutes) m12-04-restricted-namespace

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

The namespace locked enforces the restricted Pod Security Standard. The manifest ~/work/strict.yaml (the Pod strict) is rejected. Fix the manifest so that the Pod is admitted and Running: keep the image busybox:1.36 and the command, and add what the standard requires (the container must run as a non-root user, must not allow privilege escalation, must drop all capabilities, and the Pod must use the RuntimeDefault seccomp profile).

Task 5 (Design and Build, 6 points, about 6 minutes) m02-03-job-completions

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace wl, create a Job named batch with the image busybox:1.36 that runs sh -c "echo done". It must run 4 Pods to completion in total, 2 at a time (completions: 4, parallelism: 2), and be retried at most 2 times on failure (backoffLimit: 2). Wait until the Job is complete.

Task 6 (Design and Build, 6 points, about 7 minutes) m03-01-sidecar-log-tailer

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace mc, the Pod weblog (manifest ~/work/weblog.yaml) has one container app that appends lines to /var/log/app/app.log on the emptyDir volume logs. Add a sidecar container named tailer with the image busybox:1.36 that runs tail -F /var/log/app/app.log and mounts the same volume at the same path, so that kubectl logs weblog -c tailer shows the log lines. A running Pod cannot gain a container, so recreate the Pod and wait until both containers are Running.

Task 7 (Design and Build, 8 points, about 9 minutes) m04-03-pv-pvc-static

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

Create a PersistentVolume named pv-reports (capacity 2Gi, access mode ReadWriteOnce, storageClassName: manual, reclaim policy Retain, hostPath /mnt/reports). In the namespace vol, create a PersistentVolumeClaim named pvc-reports that requests 1Gi with ReadWriteOnce and storageClassName: manual, and a Pod named reporter (image busybox:1.36, command sleep 3600) that mounts the claim at /reports. The claim must be bound to pv-reports and the Pod Running.

Task 8 (Deployment, 6 points, about 6 minutes) m05-03-pause-batch-changes

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace roll, make two changes to the Deployment web in a single rollout: update its image to nginx:stable-alpine and set a memory limit of 128Mi on its container. Use kubectl rollout pause and resume so that kubectl rollout history deployment web lists exactly two revisions (1 and 2) afterwards, and wait until all replicas are Ready.

Task 9 (Deployment, 7 points, about 8 minutes) m06-02-helm-upgrade-rollback

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

The release app (chart local/webapp version 0.1.0, 1 replica) is installed in the namespace helm-ns; the repository local is already added. Upgrade the release to chart version 0.2.0 with 3 replicas. Then the upgrade turns out to be a mistake: roll the release back to its first revision. At the end the release must run chart 0.1.0 with 1 replica, and the history must show the upgrade and the rollback.

Task 10 (Deployment, 7 points, about 8 minutes) m06-06-kustomize-overlay

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

A Kustomize base exists in ~/kust/base (a Deployment web with 1 replica and a Service web). Create an overlay in ~/kust/overlays/prod that reuses the base and changes: namespace prod, a name prefix prod-, 3 replicas, and the container image to nginx:stable-alpine. Do not edit the base. Create the namespace prod, then apply the overlay to the cluster.

Task 11 (Networking, 6 points, about 6 minutes) m14-03-fix-service-selector

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace svc3, the Service api does not work: requests to http://api.svc3 hang. The Deployment api (2 replicas) is healthy. Find the cause and fix the Service without changing the Deployment, so that http://api.svc3 returns the nginx welcome page.

Task 12 (Networking, 8 points, about 8 minutes) m15-01-ingress-host-routing

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

An Ingress controller (IngressClass traefik) runs in the cluster. In the namespace ing1, the Services a and b (port 80) exist. Create an Ingress named routes that uses the class traefik and sends requests for the host a.example.com to the Service a and requests for the host b.example.com to the Service b, for all paths.

Task 13 (Networking, 7 points, about 8 minutes) m16-02-allow-from-namespace

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace np2, the Pod api (nginx, port 80) must accept TCP traffic on port 80 only from Pods in namespaces that carry the label team=frontend. Everything else must be denied. The namespace fe has the label team=frontend and the namespace other does not. Create one NetworkPolicy named api-from-frontend in np2.

Task 14 (Observability, 6 points, about 6 minutes) m07-02-fix-readiness-path

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace probes, the Pods of the Deployment web (2 replicas of nginx:alpine, which serves its page at /) never become Ready, because the readiness probe checks a path that does not exist. Fix the Deployment so that the readiness probe is an HTTP GET on path / and port 80, keep the probe, and wait until both replicas are Ready.

Task 15 (Observability, 7 points, about 8 minutes) m08-02-crashloop-env

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace dbg, the Pod of the Deployment app keeps crashing (CrashLoopBackOff). Read the container log to find the cause and fix it without changing the image or the command: the application needs the environment variable DB_URL with the value postgres://db:5432/app. Wait until the Deployment has 1 Ready replica.

Task 16 (Observability, 6 points, about 6 minutes) m08-06-fix-pending-pod

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

The Pod big in the namespace dbg (manifest ~/work/big.yaml) stays Pending. Find the reason in its events and fix the manifest so that the Pod is Running: lower the CPU request to 100m. Keep the name, image and namespace. A Pod's resources cannot be edited in place, so recreate it.

<!-- /SET -->

3Reference solutions

Open these only after the timer ends.

Solution 1: m09-01-configmap-env-volume

kubectl -n cfg create configmap app-config --from-literal=LOG_LEVEL=debug --from-literal=color=blue
kubectl -n cfg apply -f - <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: cfgpod}
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    env:
    - name: LOG_LEVEL
      valueFrom:
        configMapKeyRef: {name: app-config, key: LOG_LEVEL}
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: conf, mountPath: /etc/app}
  volumes:
  - name: conf
    configMap: {name: app-config}
Y
kubectl -n cfg wait --for=condition=Ready pod/cfgpod --timeout=120s
kubectl -n cfg exec cfgpod -- sh -c 'echo $LOG_LEVEL; cat /etc/app/color'

Solution 2: m11-03-role-rolebinding

kubectl -n auth create role pod-reader --verb=get,list,watch --resource=pods
kubectl -n auth create rolebinding read-pods --role=pod-reader --serviceaccount=auth:app-sa
kubectl -n auth auth can-i delete pods --as=system:serviceaccount:auth:app-sa
kubectl -n auth auth can-i list pods --as=system:serviceaccount:auth:app-sa

Solution 3: m10-03-resource-quota

kubectl -n quota create quota team-quota --hard=pods=3,requests.cpu=500m,limits.memory=1Gi
kubectl -n quota create deployment web --image=nginx:alpine --replicas=2 --dry-run=client -o yaml > /tmp/web.yaml
sed -i 's/^        resources: {}/        resources:\n          requests: {cpu: 100m}\n          limits: {memory: 256Mi}/' /tmp/web.yaml
kubectl apply -f /tmp/web.yaml
kubectl -n quota rollout status deployment web --timeout=120s
kubectl -n quota describe quota team-quota

Solution 4: m12-04-restricted-namespace

kubectl apply -f ~/work/strict.yaml 2>&1 | head -5
cat > ~/work/strict.yaml <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: strict
  namespace: locked
spec:
  securityContext:
    runAsNonRoot: true
    runAsUser: 10001
    seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    securityContext:
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
      capabilities:
        drop: ["ALL"]
Y
kubectl apply -f ~/work/strict.yaml
kubectl -n locked wait --for=condition=Ready pod/strict --timeout=120s

Solution 5: m02-03-job-completions

kubectl -n wl create job batch --image=busybox:1.36 --dry-run=client -o yaml -- sh -c "echo done" > /tmp/batch.yaml
sed -i 's/^spec:/spec:\n  completions: 4\n  parallelism: 2\n  backoffLimit: 2/' /tmp/batch.yaml
kubectl apply -f /tmp/batch.yaml
kubectl -n wl wait --for=condition=complete job/batch --timeout=180s

Solution 6: m03-01-sidecar-log-tailer

kubectl -n mc delete pod weblog --wait=true
cat > ~/work/weblog.yaml <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: weblog
  namespace: mc
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh", "-c", "i=0; while true; do echo log line $i >> /var/log/app/app.log; i=$((i+1)); sleep 2; done"]
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: logs, mountPath: /var/log/app}
  - name: tailer
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh", "-c", "tail -F /var/log/app/app.log"]
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: logs, mountPath: /var/log/app}
  volumes:
  - name: logs
    emptyDir: {}
Y
kubectl apply -f ~/work/weblog.yaml
kubectl -n mc wait --for=condition=Ready pod/weblog --timeout=120s
sleep 5
kubectl -n mc logs weblog -c tailer

Solution 7: m04-03-pv-pvc-static

kubectl apply -f - <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: pv-reports
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 2Gi
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: manual
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  hostPath:
    path: /mnt/reports
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: pvc-reports
  namespace: vol
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: manual
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: reporter
  namespace: vol
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: reports, mountPath: /reports}
  volumes:
  - name: reports
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: pvc-reports
Y
kubectl -n vol wait --for=condition=Ready pod/reporter --timeout=120s
kubectl -n vol get pvc

Solution 8: m05-03-pause-batch-changes

kubectl -n roll rollout pause deployment web
kubectl -n roll set image deployment web nginx=nginx:stable-alpine
kubectl -n roll set resources deployment web -c nginx --limits=memory=128Mi
kubectl -n roll rollout resume deployment web
kubectl -n roll rollout status deployment web --timeout=120s
kubectl -n roll rollout history deployment web

Solution 9: m06-02-helm-upgrade-rollback

helm upgrade app local/webapp --version 0.2.0 -n helm-ns --set replicaCount=3 --wait --timeout 120s
helm history app -n helm-ns
helm rollback app 1 -n helm-ns --wait --timeout 120s
helm history app -n helm-ns

Solution 10: m06-06-kustomize-overlay

cat > ~/kust/overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml <<'Y'
resources:
- ../../base
namespace: prod
namePrefix: prod-
replicas:
- {name: web, count: 3}
images:
- {name: nginx, newTag: stable-alpine}
Y
kubectl kustomize ~/kust/overlays/prod | head -30
kubectl create ns prod
kubectl apply -k ~/kust/overlays/prod
kubectl -n prod rollout status deployment prod-web --timeout=120s

Solution 11: m14-03-fix-service-selector

kubectl -n svc3 get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=api
kubectl -n svc3 get svc api -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'; echo
kubectl -n svc3 get pods --show-labels
kubectl -n svc3 patch svc api -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"api"}}}'

Solution 12: m15-01-ingress-host-routing

kubectl get ingressclass
kubectl -n ing1 create ingress routes --class=traefik --rule="a.example.com/*=a:80" --rule="b.example.com/*=b:80"
kubectl -n ing1 get ingress routes
sleep 5

Solution 13: m16-02-allow-from-namespace

kubectl -n np2 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: {name: api-from-frontend}
spec:
  podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: api}}
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector: {matchLabels: {team: frontend}}
    ports:
    - {protocol: TCP, port: 80}
Y
sleep 5

Solution 14: m07-02-fix-readiness-path

kubectl -n probes describe pod -l app=web | grep -i "readiness"
kubectl -n probes patch deployment web --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe/httpGet/path","value":"/"}]'
kubectl -n probes rollout status deployment web --timeout=120s

Solution 15: m08-02-crashloop-env

kubectl -n dbg get pods
kubectl -n dbg logs deploy/app --tail=5
kubectl -n dbg set env deployment app DB_URL=postgres://db:5432/app
kubectl -n dbg rollout status deployment app --timeout=120s

Solution 16: m08-06-fix-pending-pod

kubectl -n dbg describe pod big | tail -5
kubectl -n dbg delete pod big --wait=true
sed -i 's/cpu: "100"/cpu: 100m/' ~/work/big.yaml
kubectl apply -f ~/work/big.yaml
kubectl -n dbg wait --for=condition=Ready pod/big --timeout=120s

<!-- /SETSOL -->

4Review after the set

  • Count your points per domain and compare them with the pass mark of 66 percent.
  • Write every reading mistake (wrong namespace, wrong name, missing context line) on your personal checklist.
  • Redo the tasks you flagged or failed, this time with the reference solution closed.
  • Do Set B a few days later, under the same conditions.

5Recall questions

R1How many points do you need to pass the set, and what is the passing score of the exam?

Show the answer

66% of the points, the same as the exam.

R2What is the first action on every task?

Show the answer

Run the context line and note the exact names and namespaces.

R3What do you do with a task that is stuck after about six minutes?

Show the answer

Flag it, move on and return at the end.

R4Which command shows why a Pod is Pending or crashing?

Show the answer

kubectl describe pod, then kubectl logs (--previous after a restart).

R5Which two flags generate YAML without creating the object?

Show the answer

--dry-run=client -o yaml.

R6How do you confirm that a Service has working backends?

Show the answer

kubectl get endpoints <service> and a test request from a throw-away Pod.

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Time 120 minutes, about 6 to 8 minutes per task
Pass 66% of the points; tasks are all-or-nothing
Order easy first, flag the hard ones, keep time to verify
Verify a second command (get, describe, logs, a test request)
After the set repeat the tasks you flagged, then the other set
